questions.questionText: How does spear phishing differ from generic mass phishing?

options.text: Spear phishing is automated using pop-up advertisements
Spear phishing is highly targeted at a specific individual or team using researched details
Spear phishing only targets mobile phones using text messages
Spear phishing requires physical entry into an office building

questions.explanation: Spear phishing relies on prior reconnaissance to tailor realistic messages directly to specific targets.

questions.questionText: Public professional profiles on LinkedIn can provide attackers with information used to craft spear phishing messages.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Attackers mine job titles, reporting structures, vendor software, and current projects from LinkedIn profiles to build convincing pretexts.

questions.questionText: Why do attackers often send password-protected .zip files containing malicious attachments?

options.text: To save hard drive storage space on remote laptops
To prevent email security gateways from scanning the encrypted contents for malware
To make the file download faster over home Wi-Fi networks
Because password protection automatically executes scripts

questions.explanation: Email gateway scanners cannot inspect encrypted archive contents without the password, allowing malicious payloads past boundary defenses.

questions.questionText: Which public sources are commonly harvested by adversaries during the OSINT phase of a spear phishing campaign? (Select ALL that apply)

options.text: LinkedIn corporate organizational charts
Public GitHub code repositories detailing software libraries
Personal social media posts detailing travel or conference attendance
Encrypted database servers operating behind private firewalls

questions.explanation: LinkedIn, GitHub, and social media posts provide open public data. Private encrypted database servers are not public OSINT sources.

questions.questionText: Spear phishers only target executives; entry-level remote contractors are never targeted because they lack system permissions.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Entry-level contractors are frequently targeted as initial access points to pivot deeper into enterprise networks or harvest credentials.

questions.questionText: Reducing the amount of detailed operational information shared on public social media accounts helps reduce your exposure to OSINT reconnaissance.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Practicing digital footprint hygiene limits the intelligence attackers can use to build spear phishing lures.

questions.questionText: An email claiming to be from your company's HR department contains a link to “Updated W-2 Tax Forms.” The link URL points to an external domain unrelated to your company. What is the safest course of action?

options.text: Click the link and enter your Social Security Number.
Hover over the link, identify the external domain, do not click, and report it to security/HR.
Email your password to HR to check for you.
Ignore all future HR emails forever.

questions.explanation: Identifying external, non-company domain names by hovering over links helps detect phishing portals before entering credentials.

questions.questionText: Spear phishing relies solely on technical software exploits and does not use psychological manipulation.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Spear phishing is a socio-technical attack combining technical delivery vectors with psychological manipulation (trust, urgency, authority).

questions.questionText: What step should you take before opening a password-protected .zip file from an external party?

options.text: Open it on a personal device to protect work systems.
Verify the source out-of-band and inspect unzipped contents in an isolated environment or sandbox.
Forward the password to your bank.
Disable your endpoint firewall.

questions.explanation: Verifying the source through another channel and inspecting files securely prevents payload execution.

questions.questionText: What information can an attacker gather from your public GitHub profile to make a spear-phishing email believable?

options.text: Your private home Wi-Fi password
Programming languages used, active repositories, and collaborator usernames
Your hardware MFA seed keys
Your credit card PIN

questions.explanation: Public GitHub repositories display technical environments, active projects, and peer collaborators.
